title: [Risk prediction of pneumonia in maintenance hemodialysis patients after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection].
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the risk factors for pneumonia after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2(SARS-CoV-2) infection in maintenance hemodialysis patients from a single center in China, and to establish a multivariate model to predict the risk of pneumonia. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on maintenance hemodialysis patients with positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen or nucleic acid tests treated at Peking University Third Hospital from December 1, 2022 to January 31, 2023. Demographic data, comorbidities, dialysis-related parameters, and laboratory test results were collected. Multivariate Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve were adopted to explore risk factors of pneumonia, and a multivariate model was established to predict the risk of pneumonia occurrence. title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models. RESULTS: P P for interaction for interaction In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (<0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80],<0.05). CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

title: Targeting Nupr1-Mediated p53 Mitochondrial Sequestration Alleviates Aortic Dissection by Restoring the Gadd45b-Dependent Survival Program.
abstract: Aortic dissection (AD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency triggered by severe pathological stress. While continuous stress drives vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) apoptosis via mitochondrial dysfunction, the precise upstream orchestrators linking these stress signals to the mitochondrial apoptotic cascade remain elusive. By integrating clinical observations and single-cell RNA sequencing, we found that Nuclear Protein 1 (Nupr1), a critical stress-responsive factor, is significantly upregulated in aortas from AD patients and murine models, with enrichment in VSMCs. Remarkably, VSMC-specific Nupr1 deficiency significantly ameliorated AD progression in vivo. Mechanistically, Nupr1 undergoes massive mitochondrial accumulation in Ang II-induced apoptotic VSMCs. Rather than operating as a conventional transcriptional regulator, mitochondrially enriched Nupr1 functions as a pathological spatial switch. It sequesters p53 within mitochondria, driving transcription-independent apoptosis while simultaneously blunting the protective Gadd45b-mediated survival program. Furthermore, in vivo Gadd45b overexpression was sufficient to rescue mitochondrial dysfunction and ameliorate vascular collapse. Taken together, our findings conceptualize the Nupr1-p53-Gadd45b axis as an important determinant of VSMC fate and provide a novel and promising therapeutic strategy for preventing AD progression.

title: Successful First-Line Haploidentical Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in an Elderly Patient With Severe Aplastic Anemia and Complex Comorbidities: A Case Report.
abstract: Standard management guidelines generally recommend immunosuppressive therapy (IST) as first-line treatment for older patients with severe aplastic anemia (SAA), whereas the role of upfront haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (haplo-HSCT) in this population remains uncertain, particularly in patients with complex comorbidities. We report a 62-year-old woman with SAA, a history of surgically resected stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, and previous left lower extremity deep vein thrombosis treated with venous stent implantation and long-term aspirin therapy. Because no matched sibling or unrelated donor was available, and following individualized counseling regarding IST and transplantation, the patient underwent upfront haplo-HSCT combined with umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells after a conditioning regimen including fludarabine, busulfan, cyclophosphamide, antithymocyte globulin, and thiotepa. Neutrophil engraftment occurred on post-transplant day +12, and platelet independence was achieved on day +13. Donor chimerism reached 99.6% by day +14 and remained within the complete-chimerism range through the latest available assessment in January 2026. In late December 2025 and January 2026, the patient developed cytomegalovirus infection accompanied by transient trilineage cytopenia; after anti-CMV treatment with maribavir, the infection was controlled and peripheral blood counts subsequently recovered. At the most recent clinical follow-up on August 6, 2026, approximately 17 months after transplantation, no chronic graft-versus-host disease had developed, the previous lung adenocarcinoma remained in remission, and the thrombotic condition remained clinically stable. This case suggests that upfront haplo-HSCT combined with UC-MSCs may represent a feasible individualized treatment option for carefully selected older patients with SAA who lack matched donors, although broader conclusions require larger studies and longer follow-up.

title: Efficacy and Safety of No Thromboprophylaxis after Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation for Incompetent Saphenous VeiNs: the TRAIN Non-inferiority Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The benefit of post-operative pharmacological thromboprophylaxis after endovenous radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for incompetent saphenous veins in patients without previous deep vein thrombosis (DVT) of the lower limbs is unclear. This trial compared no extended thromboprophylaxis with extended anticoagulation after RFA. METHODS: TRAIN (Thromboprophylaxis after endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation for Incompetent saphenous veiNs) was a multicentre, evaluator blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial. Adults with primary great saphenous vein incompetence undergoing RFA, with concomitant tributary phlebectomy and or ultrasound guided foam sclerotherapy when clinically indicated, were enrolled. Patients with previous DVT of the lower limbs were excluded. All participants received a single intra-operative intravenous dose of unfractionated heparin and were randomised to either no extended pharmacological thromboprophylaxis or rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for fourteen days post-operatively. The primary outcome was thrombosis related events within thirty days. RESULTS: Of 406 patients screened, 354 were included in the intention to treat analysis and 304 in the per protocol analysis. The no extended thromboprophylaxis strategy was non-inferior to fourteen days of rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for thrombosis related events (risk difference -1.34%, 95% confidence interval -7.53 - 4.84%; p = .022 for non-inferiority). One participant in the anticoagulation group (one of 177; 0.6%) experienced clinically relevant non-major bleeding on post-operative day 10. No bleeding event occurred in the no anticoagulation group (0 of 177; p = 1.0). CONCLUSION: Omitting extended post-operative rivaroxaban thromboprophylaxis after RFA with concomitant phlebectomy and sclerotherapy in patients without previous DVT was non-inferior to fourteen days of rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for thrombosis related events. Prophylactic rivaroxaban was not associated with an increased risk of bleeding.

title: Lived experiences of post-traumatic growth in patients with acute type A aortic dissection: A qualitative study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute type A aortic dissection is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency characterized by sudden onset, severe pain, and high mortality, exerting profound physical and psychological burdens on affected individuals. While negative psychological sequelae predominate in most cases, a subset of patients demonstrates remarkable resilience, manifesting post-traumatic growth-a positive psychological transformation emerging in the aftermath of trauma. This qualitative study aimed to investigate the lived experiences of post-traumatic growth among Acute type A aortic dissection survivors, shedding light on this understudied dimension of their recovery trajectory. METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted using a phenomenological approach. Twenty patients diagnosed with Acute type A aortic dissection were recruited through purposive sampling from a tertiary hospital in China. Data were collected via in-depth, face-to-face semi-structured interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step method to extract key themes and sub-themes. RESULTS: Three overarching themes and eight sub-themes were identified, reflecting the multidimensional nature of post-traumatic growth in Acute type A aortic dissection patients: Reevaluating Life Priorities (reordering life priorities, valuing life), Behavioral Transformation (improving unhealthy habits, enhancing treatment adherence), and Enhanced Social Connections (strengthened family ties, gratitude for social support, reintegration into family and society, altruistic behavior). CONCLUSIONS: This study elucidates three core dimensions of post-traumatic growth in survivors of acute type A aortic dissection: life priority reassessment, adoption of positive health behaviors, and enhanced social connectedness. The findings underscore the critical role of guided self-reflection, supported behavior change, and robust family-social support systems in facilitating psychological recovery. We recommend integrating interventions focused on post-traumatic growth, such as psychological counseling and structured family support, into standard cardiac rehabilitation protocols to promote holistic recovery. Together, these insights provide a theoretical and practical foundation for developing tailored psychosocial interventions for this patient population.

title: Prior Venous Thromboembolism Defines Distinct Genetic and Molecular Phenotypes in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) has traditionally been considered a long-term complication of pulmonary embolism. However, a substantial proportion of patients have no history of venous thromboembolism (VTE), suggesting underlying biological heterogeneity. METHODS: We analyzed clinical and imaging characteristics of 712 patients with CTEPH stratified by prior VTE history. Whole-genome sequencing was performed in all patients and 2952 healthy controls to assess common variants. Bulk RNA sequencing of pulmonary endarterectomy tissues and plasma protein quantification were integrated to identify and validate subgroup-specific molecular signatures, with further validation in tissue and primary endothelial cells. RESULTS: ABO P FGG P P CTSS CTSS -9 -8 Patients with CTEPH and prior VTE (n=576, 80.9%) exhibited a distinct thrombotic phenotype with more proximal disease distribution (92.5% versus 66.2%) and greater likelihood of undergoing pulmonary endarterectomy (22.6% versus 3.7%). Genome-wide association study in CTEPH-VTE(+) patients versus controls identified coagulation-related loci at(rs676996,=1.1×10) and(rs7681423,=2.5×10), with high genetic correlation with pulmonary embolism (rg=0.52,=0.028). In contrast, no consistent genomic signal was identified in patients without prior VTE. Integrative multiomics (transcriptome-wide association study, MAGMA, and bulk RNA sequencing differential expression analysis) convergently prioritized(cathepsin S) as a key molecular candidate in CTEPH-VTE(+). title: Identification of perioperative risk factors for retrograde type A dissection after thoracic endovascular aortic repair for type B dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify risk factors and develop a predictive model for retrograde type A dissection (RTAD) following thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHODS: We analyzed TBAD patients who underwent TEVAR from 2014 to 2024 (IRB:No. TJ-IRB20230805). Patients developing RTAD within 1 year were matched with controls by age, sex, operation date, and location. Logistic regression identified risk factors, and a nomogram was constructed. Model performance was assessed using ROC curves. RESULTS: p p p p p p Of 2383 patients, 76 (3.19%) developed RTAD within one year. 65 RTAD cases and 195 matched controls were analyzed. RTAD patients had a greater horizontal distance of the ascending aorta (HDAA) than controls (53.34 mm vs. 43.05 mm, < .001). Multivariate analysis identified younger age (OR = 0.95, = .008), larger HDAA (OR = 1.14, < .001), aortic root dilatation (OR = 2.85, = .006), shorter stent length (OR = 0.99, = .029), and absence of postoperative bradycardic drug use (OR = 0.31, = .005) as independent RTAD risk factors. The model showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.85). CONCLUSION: Younger age, larger HDAA, aortic root dilatation, shorter stent length, and no bradycardic drugs postoperatively are independent predictors of RTAD after TEVAR. For TBAD patients with a high risk of RTAD, clinicians should consider the possibility of having connective tissue diseases, select stents appropriately, and optimize postoperative treatment with strict follow-up.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Intraosseous Regional Versus Intravenous Tranexamic Acid in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tranexamic acid (TXA) reduces perioperative blood loss in total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, evidence for intraosseous regional administration (IORA) remains limited. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of IORA-TXA versus intravenous TXA (IV-TXA) in TKA. METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, single-center trial, 98 patients undergoing primary TKA were randomized 1:1 to IORA-TXA or IV-TXA (49 per group) at a uniform dose of 20 mg/kg. The primary outcome was calculated perioperative blood loss. Secondary efficacy outcomes included calculated hidden blood loss, postoperative hemoglobin (Hb) levels, and transfusion rate. Safety outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular calf vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism (PE), and wound-related complications. RESULTS: Compared with IV-TXA, IORA-TXA reduced calculated perioperative blood loss (674.8 ± 335.0 vs. 817.5 ± 357.2 mL; mean difference, 142.6 mL; 95% CI, 7.4-277.8; p = 0.038) and calculated hidden blood loss (644.8 ± 335.5 vs. 790.9 ± 339.0 mL; mean difference, 146.1 mL; 95% CI, 10.9-281.3; p = 0.035). Postoperative Hb was similar on POD1 (134.0 ± 9.8 vs. 130.1 ± 11.1 g/L; p = 0.067) but was higher with IORA-TXA on POD2 (119.8 ± 8.3 vs. 113.8 ± 11.5 g/L; mean difference 6.0 g/L; 95% CI 2.0-10.0; p = 0.005) and POD3 (114.8 ± 7.9 vs. 109.8 ± 12.6 g/L; mean difference 5.0 g/L; 95% CI 0.8-9.2; p = 0.020). No patient required blood transfusion. title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction. OBJECTIVE: To conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluating the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD. METHODS: Following PRISMA/PRISMA-S guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and PROBAST risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary ROC (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with GRADE. RESULTS: 2 Ten studies were included. The pooled AUC for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I= 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.855 and specificity 0.836. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than non-registry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; p = 0.004). All models had high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low. CONCLUSIONS: ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to AI reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.

title: Association between increased superficial calcification clusters in carotid atherosclerosis and cardiovascular events after carotid artery stenting: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) was conducted via outpatient visits and telephone. Ultimately, 211 subjects completed 2-year follow-up. Superficial calcification clusters were counted on CTA. Subjects with ≥4 superficial calcification clusters (n=24) were matched in a 1:4 ratio to those with <4 superficial calcification clusters (n=96). Sensitivity analysis was performed based on the matched cohort. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 1.92 years, 14 MACEs occurring more than 30 days after discharge were recorded. In univariate Cox analysis, symptom status (P= 0.0116), alcohol abuse (P= 0.0091), total number of calcification clusters (P= 0.0428), and number of superficial calcification clusters (P= 0.0022) were significantly associated with MACEs. In bivariate analyses, the number of superficial calcification clusters maintained a reasonably good association with MACEs. In sensitivity analysis, superficial calcification clusters remained significantly associated with MACE when loss to follow-up was classified as MACE (P= 0.0256, HR= 1.2548, 95% CI 1.0281-1.5315) or as no MACE (P= 0.0265, HR= 1.4948, 95% CI 1.0479-2.1323). CONCLUSION: The number of superficial calcification clusters may independently serve as a prognostic risk factor in patients with carotid atherosclerosis undergoing CAS.

title: Clinical Outcomes and Exploratory Haemodynamic Numerical Simulation of Patients with Multichannelled Aortic Dissection: A Multicentre, Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Multichannelled aortic dissection (MCAD) is a rare type of aortic dissection with limited data on its clinical features and outcomes. This multicentre, retrospective cohort study compared clinical outcomes between MCAD and double channelled aortic dissection (DCAD) and explored haemodynamic differences. METHODS: Patients with aortic dissection were enrolled from three tertiary hospitals. Patients with one true lumen and one false lumen were classified as having DCAD, whereas those with one true lumen and multiple false lumina were classified as having MCAD. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics. Primary outcomes were 30 day and five year all cause mortality after diagnosis. Secondary outcomes included preprocedural mortality, aortic dissection related mortality, post-operative complications, and re-intervention. Overall survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Haemodynamic differences were evaluated by exploratory computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis. RESULTS: After matching, 50 patients were included in each group (n = 100). The difference in 30 day mortality was significant (p = .046) and largely reflected preprocedural deaths, which occurred in six patients with MCAD (12%) and none with DCAD (p = .027). Overall survival differed between groups (log rank p = .037; hazard ratio 2.72, 95% confidence interval 1.03 - 7.18; p = .044). Kaplan-Meier estimated mortality at 30 days, one year, and five years was 16%, 23%, and 29% in MCAD compared with 4%, 8%, and 12% in DCAD, respectively. Among treated patients, re-intervention was more frequent in MCAD than in DCAD (21% vs. 6%; p = .036), whereas post-operative complication rates did not differ. Exploratory CFD analysis suggested greater false lumen haemodynamic burden in MCAD. CONCLUSION: MCAD was associated with greater preprocedural mortality and more frequent re-intervention than DCAD. These findings may identify MCAD as a higher risk phenotype warranting closer surveillance and timely evaluation. Haemodynamic observations remain exploratory and require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Progress on the related mechanisms of vascular calcification in autogenous arteriovenous fistula in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for end-stage renal disease patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis as a replacement therapy. As the duration of dialysis increases, the risk of vascular access-related complications such as AVF stenosis, thrombosis, vascular calcification (VC), and aneurysm formation gradually rises. Among these, VC has been proven to be independently associated with the occurrence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). VC in the AVF of dialysis patients can lead to AVF failure, severely limiting its usability and increasing the risk of mortality among dialysis patients. Unlike previous reviews that predominantly focused on isolated mechanisms such as mineral metabolism or arterial calcification, this narrative review innovatively integrates the crosstalk among hemodynamic stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, deficiency of endogenous calcification inhibitors and pathological matrix remodeling, thereby providing a multidimensional perspective on AVF-VC. This review reframes the current understanding of AVF-VC, shifting it from a generalized complication of CKD-mineral and bone disorder to a distinct, fistula-specific pathological entity. This conceptual advancement offers a theoretical foundation for developing precision intervention strategies tailored to the unique microenvironment of the AVF.

title: Combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches for embolization of a traumatic carotid‑cavernous fistula with concomitant middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula.
abstract: Endovascular treatment (EVT) is a useful modality for traumatic carotid‑cavernous fistulas (CCFs); in rare cases, combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches may be applied for embolization of the fistula with concomitant internal carotid artery (ICA) sacrifice and preservation of the ophthalmic artery (OphA). A 62‑year‑old female patient sustained a motor vehicle accident and developed proptosis, chemosis, and congestion in her right eye, while no abnormalities in ocular motility or visual acuity were noted. Computed tomography angiography confirmed the CCF. Under general anesthesia, digital subtraction angiography revealed a right CCF supplied antegradely by the ICA and retrogradely by the posterior communicating artery (PcomA). A left middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula was identified. Access to the basilar artery was established. A microcatheter was retrogradely navigated via the PcomA to reach the proximal ICA across the fistula. Then, another microcatheter was advanced into the cavernous sinus via an antegrade ICA approach. Subsequently, combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial coiling with ICA sacrifice for the CCF was successfully performed. During coiling, the patency of the OphA was monitored through the PcomA microcatheter. Afterwards, the middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula was embolized. At the 1‑month follow‑up, her right eye redness and swelling resolved, and at the 3‑month follow‑up, she had recovered well and returned to her normal status. Therefore, when embolizing the CCF with ICA sacrifice, if the PcomA is well‑developed, the combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches can be used, which may facilitate the obliteration of the CCF and preservation of the OphA.

title: A thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor: A case report.
abstract: Thoracic SWI/SNF-related BAF chromatin remodeling complex subunit ATPase 4 (SMARCA4)-deficient undifferentiated tumor (SMARCA4-UT) is a newly recognized, high-grade malignant neoplasm that is rare in clinical practice. There is no standardized or clearly defined treatment protocol for SMARCA4-UT in clinical guidelines. The current study reports the case of a 54-year-old male patient who presented with a 2-month history of an intermittent productive cough. Bronchoscopy demonstrated a neoplasm in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe bronchus, which almost obstructed the lumen, with a hypervascular surface, suggestive of a right upper lobe carcinoma. Histopathological examination confirmed a poorly differentiated carcinoma. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated a SMARCA4 gene mutation in exon 4, classifying the tumor as SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated lung carcinoma. The patient developed superior vena cava syndrome (SVCS), requiring emergent percutaneous stent placement. Treatment also included computed tomography-guided cryoablation and radiofrequency ablation (RFA), alongside targeted molecular therapy with crizotinib. Despite aggressive multimodal therapy, the patient succumbed to tumor thrombosis at 1 month post-treatment. Overall, SMARCA4-UT is rare and diagnostically challenging, lacking standardized treatment guidelines. In clinical practice, cryoablation with argon-helium and RFA may provide palliative benefits by alleviating tumor burden and improving quality of life. Endovascular intervention provides a rapid and effective approach to alleviate tumor-induced SVCS. However, subsequent anticoagulation and antineoplastic therapies require further investigation to determine their efficacy in the management of such cases.

title: SHR-2004, a Humanized Monoclonal Antibody Targeting Factor XI, for Preventing Venous Thromboembolism After Ovarian Cancer Surgery: A Randomized, Active-Controlled Phase 2 Study.
abstract: This multicenter, randomized, open-label, exploratory Phase 2 trial assessed SHR-2004, an anti-FXI antibody, for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention in patients undergoing ovarian cancer surgery-a population at particularly high thrombotic risk conducted at 25 sites in China. Patients with newly diagnosed Stage III-IV or recurrent ovarian cancer scheduled for surgery were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive subcutaneous SHR-2004 (180 mg on Day 1 and 120 mg on Day 15) or enoxaparin-rivaroxaban (subcutaneous enoxaparin 40 mg once daily during hospitalization, followed by oral rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily after discharge until Day 28). The primary efficacy outcome was the composite of VTE events within 28 days. The primary safety outcome was major bleeding (MB) or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (CRNMB) from first dose to 28 days. Between February 19, 2024 and September 17, 2024, 198 patients received assigned treatment (90 with SHR-2004, 108 with enoxaparin-rivaroxaban) and were included in the safety analysis. Among 181 patients who completed protocol-mandated ultrasonography, VTE occurred in 11 (12.6%) patients in the SHR-2004 group and 19 (20.2%) in the enoxaparin-rivaroxaban group (difference -8.4%, 95% CI -19.9 to 3.1) by Day 28. MB/CRNMB rates were similar between groups (SHR-2004: 2/90 [2.2%]; enoxaparin-rivaroxaban: 2/108 [1.9%]). In this study, SHR-2004 showed comparable efficacy to enoxaparin-rivaroxaban for preventing postoperative VTE in patients undergoing ovarian cancer surgery, with a similar low risk of MB or CRNMB. The twice-monthly dosing schedule offers a potential advantage over daily anticoagulation, supporting further investigation in adequately powered Phase 3 trials. title: The Imaging Compass: Navigating Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: The management of acute ischemic stroke has shifted from rigid time-based protocols to imaging-driven, tissue-based reperfusion strategies. Non-contrast CT and CT angiography remain the indispensable frontline for rapid triage, particularly in community and low-resource settings. However, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides unique biological information that complements CT-based assessment: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) detects cellular ischemia within minutes without contrast; DWI-fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) mismatch serves as a tissue clock for unknown-onset stroke; susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) aids thrombus characterization; and MRI resolves the posterior fossa without beam-hardening artifact. Low-field portable MRI further extends these capabilities to the bedside where conventional scanners are unavailable. This review examines four convergent trends within this transition: expanding thrombectomy to large-core infarction, extending thrombolysis through tissue-based selection, advancing recanalization in posterior-circulation stroke while defining boundaries for medium- and distal-vessel occlusions, and simplifying imaging workflows through fast MRI protocols, quantitative CT biomarkers, and artificial intelligence (AI). Landmark trials have established that treatment benefit is determined by tissue viability rather than clock time, while recent negative trials define critical boundaries beyond which intervention may cause harm. We critically appraise how CT and MRI are integrated hierarchically across these scenarios, and how emerging fast MRI and quantitative biomarkers may reshape future selection paradigms. title: Machine learning-derived serum carbon dioxide trajectories in predicting prognosis of patients with acute aortic dissection.
abstract: Venous partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PvCO 2 ) indicates postoperative adverse outcomes in patients with acute aortic dissection, and its trajectories over time affecting postoperative adverse outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PvCO 2 trajectories and postoperative adverse outcomes, as well as clinical application through group-based trajectory modeling and machine-learning algorithms. This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from 642 patients with acute aortic dissection treated at the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University from 2019 to 2024, to determine postoperative adverse outcomes, including 6-month mortality and complications. Three PvCO 2 tests within the first 72 hours of admission were used to analyze PvCO 2 trajectories through group-based trajectory modeling. To diagnose high-risk PvCO 2 trajectories in emergency settings, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was conducted to select key features, which were consequently integrated into predictive models using multiple machine-learning methods. Finally, a web-based interpretable website was developed for predicting PvCO 2 trajectories in patients with acute aortic dissection. Overall, 642 patients were classed into four PvCO 2 trajectories (T1, persistent decrease from a medium to a low level; T2, stable low level; T3, persistent decrease from a high to a low level; T4, stable midlevel), showing distinct patterns. After adjustment for other covariates, postoperative adverse outcomes among these groups showed significant differences, with a higher proportion of postoperative adverse outcomes in the T3 group. Subsequently, upon Shapley additive explanations analysis, 17 features with importance sequence were identified (hemoglobin, direct bilirubin, monocyte, adenosine deaminase, drinking, anion gap, chloride, platelet, lymphocyte, albumin/globulin ratio, calcium, alanine aminotransferase, α-L-fucosidase, D-dimer, antihypertensive drugs, and smoking), which were integrated into the model for predicting T3. The optimal machine-learning model was established for predicting postoperative adverse outcomes. Finally, a web-based interpretable model was developed to predict patients with acute aortic dissection and high risk of postoperative adverse outcomes. This study uncovers heterogeneity in PvCO 2 trajectory, highlighting that decreased PvCO 2 is associated with worse prognosis. A web-based tool for the prediction of acute aortic dissection patients at high risk of postoperative adverse outcomes was constructed to facilitate clinical application.

title: Factors associated with patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The factors influencing patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting remain incompletely understood. We therefore conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize the available evidence. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched to December 2025. Studies reporting associations between potential risk factors and stent outcomes were included. Data were synthesized narratively, and random-effects meta-analyses with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed when comparable multivariable-adjusted estimates were available. RESULTS: A total of 49 studies were included, predominantly involving retrospective cohorts. The meta-analysis suggested that post-thrombotic disease, stent extension across or below the inguinal ligament, and hyperlipidemia were associated with an increased risk of patency loss, whereas increasing age showed a modest inverse association with patency loss. The narrative evidence suggested that greater anatomical disease extent was associated with poorer stent patency, whereas the evidence regarding impaired venous inflow was heterogeneous and varied according to the disease phenotype, anatomical segment, and inflow definition. Pooled analyses did not identify statistically significant associations of sex, stent length, or number of stents with patency loss. Evidence regarding anticoagulation discontinuation and adjunctive antiplatelet therapy was insufficient and inconsistent. CONCLUSIONS: Patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting appears to be associated with the disease phenotype, higher anatomical disease burden, and stent landing strategy. Venous inflow impairment may also be associated with poorer stent patency, although the evidence was heterogeneous. The predominantly retrospective evidence precludes causal inference. Prospective studies with standardized definitions and robust adjustment are needed to improve risk stratification and optimize post-stenting management.

title: Key factors for predicting outcomes one year after Meso-Rex bypass surgery and optimizing the surgical plan in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To analyze the factors for predicting 1-year outcomes and optimize surgical planning for Meso-Rex bypass (MRB) in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO). MATERIALS AND METHODS: From October 2014 to July 2024, children with EHPVO after MRB were retrospectively analyzed. The number of MRB, the type of bypass vessel, and the position of the lower anastomosis were collected. Predictive variables include the diameter of the connection between the left and right portal veins, the Rex vein (RV) diameter, the number of RV branches, the diameter of the thickest RV branch, and the bypass-to-superior mesenteric vein (SMV) angle, which were measured by Contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) one week after MRB. The upper and lower anastomotic stenosis were diagnosed by Ultrasound and CECT one year after MRB. RESULTS: A total of 153 children (median age 72 months, 87 males) were included in this study. Univariate factors include the number of MRBs, the type of bypass vessel, and CECT variables (except the diameter of the thickest RV branch). Numbers of MRB and RV branches were retained in the final model for upper anastomotic stenosis. The combination of MRB > 1 and RV branches ≤ 4 predicts it post-MRB with 75% sensitivity, 86.4% specificity, and an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.832. The bypass-to-SMV angle ≤ 110° predicts lower anastomotic stenosis after MRB with 90% sensitivity, 73.39% specificity, and AUC 0.847. CONCLUSIONS: Associated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the type of bypass vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle could be used to inform future surgical technique refinement. Clinical RelevanceAssociated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the internal jugular vein as the bridge vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle > 110° could be used to optimize the surgical plan for a better outcome.

title: Adjunctive citrus flavonoids after endovenous microwave ablation for great saphenous vein varicosis: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adjunctive citrus flavonoids are associated with improved venous hemodynamics and short-term outcomes after endovenous microwave ablation (EMA) for great saphenous vein varicosis in a retrospective cohort. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 254 patients with great saphenous vein varicosis treated between January 2022 and July 2025. Patients were grouped according to the actual treatment received: EMA alone (n = 126) or EMA plus micronized purified flavonoid fraction (MPFF; n = 128). In the combination group, MPFF was administered at 1000 mg twice daily (2000 mg/d) for 2 weeks; this was twice the usual approved dose for venolymphatic insufficiency. The primary outcome was overall clinical response at 2 weeks. Secondary outcomes included Venous Clinical Severity Score, Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire, Chronic Venous Insufficiency Questionnaire, venous hemodynamic parameters, exploratory endothelial biomarkers (such as endothelin-1, nitric oxide, and circulating endothelial cells), treatment-related adverse events, and 6-month ultrasound findings. RESULTS: Compared with EMA alone, adjunctive MPFF was associated with a higher overall clinical response and greater improvements in Venous Clinical Severity Score, Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire, and Chronic Venous Insufficiency Questionnaire scores (all P < .05). Mean and peak venous flow velocities improved more in the combination group (P < .05). The combination group also showed lower endothelin-1 and circulating endothelial cell levels and higher nitric oxide levels after treatment (P < .05). Recorded adverse events did not differ significantly between groups (P > .05). At 6 months, the combination group showed a higher rate of complete occlusion and less residual reflux (P < .05). CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, adjunctive citrus flavonoids after EMA were associated with better early symptom scores, venous hemodynamic indices, and endothelial biomarker profiles without a detected increase in recorded adverse events. As the study was observational and used a nonstandard MPFF dose, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causality, proof of safety, or support for the 2000 mg/d regimen. Prospective randomized trials using approved dosing are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Omega-3 fatty acids, specialized pro-resolving mediators, and depression: A mechanistic meta-analysis of precursors and clinical implications.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFAs), especially eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), exhibit adjunctive antidepressant efficacy despite negligible detectable levels in the brain. Emerging evidence implicates specialized pro‑resolving mediators (SPMs); bioactive n-3 PUFA metabolites offer a coherent pathway by actively resolving inflammation, enhancing tissue repair, and supporting neuronal function. To test whether n‑3 PUFA supplementation activates pro‑resolving biology in humans, this meta‑analysis quantified effects on circulating SPM precursors. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, GOED, and the Cochrane Library (up to May 18, 2026) to identify RCTs examining the impact of n-3 PUFAs supplementation on circulating SPM precursors 18-hydroxyeicosapentaenoic acid (18-HEPE) and 17-hydroxydocosahexaenoic acid (17-HDHA). Meta-analysis was performed using Review Manager 5.4.1 with random-effects models. RESULTS: Eleven RCTs, comprising 810 participants, were included. N-3 PUFAs supplementation significantly and robustly increased the concentrations of both circulating SPM precursors: 18-HEPE (SMD = 1.05, 95% CI 0.54-1.55, Z = 4.08, P = 0.0001) and 17-HDHA (SMD = 0.69, 95% CI 0.19-1.18, Z = 2.72, P = 0.006). Importantly, subgroup analyses revealed that this increase was selectively amplified in patient populations characterized by a significant inflammatory, metabolic, and oxidative burden, including peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), MDD with comorbid obesity, and pregnancy, but was negligible in healthy infants. CONCLUSION: N-3 PUFA supplementation significantly increased circulating 18-HEPE and 17-HDHA, indicating greater availability of upstream EPA- and DHA-derived SPM precursors across mixed human populations. However, whether these precursor changes translate into increased downstream SPM production or clinical antidepressant effects remains uncertain and requires dedicated trials in MDD populations. title: Open- versus closed-cell stents in transfemoral carotid artery stenting for carotid bifurcation disease: a target trial emulation.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The comparative association of open-cell stent (OCS) and closed-cell stent (CCS) design with outcomes after protected transfemoral carotid artery stenting, particularly long-term patency, remains uncertain. This study compared OCSs and CCSs in patients with carotid bifurcation disease. METHODS: We retrospectively emulated a target trial using data from three centers. Consecutive patients who underwent transfemoral carotid artery stenting with embolic protection devices for atherosclerotic carotid bifurcation lesions were included and classified according to stent design. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to balance baseline covariates. Periprocedural outcomes were assessed within 30 days. Follow-up outcomes included in-stent restenosis (ISR), severe ISR, symptomatic ISR, recurrent ipsilateral ischemic events (stroke or transient ischemic attack), and target-vessel revascularization. RESULTS: Among 1024 patients, 524 (51.2%) were symptomatic and 500 (48.8%) were asymptomatic; 577 received OCSs and 447 received CCSs. Median follow-up was 26.0 months (interquartile range, 19.4-32.4 months). After inverse probability of treatment weighting, baseline covariates were well balanced. Periprocedural adverse events did not differ significantly between groups. During follow-up, CCS use was associated with higher risks of ISR (hazard ratio [HR], 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.19-2.31; P = .003), severe ISR (HR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.06-2.45; P = .026), symptomatic ISR (HR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.20-3.45; P = .008), and recurrent transient ischemic attack (HR, 3.06; 95% CI, 1.24-7.55; P = .015). Any ISR and severe ISR were strongly associated with recurrent ipsilateral ischemic events (both P < .001). CCS use appeared more strongly associated with ISR in symptomatic patients, without significant interaction by symptom status (P for interaction = .206). Sensitivity analyses were concordant with the primary results. CONCLUSIONS: OCSs were associated with a lower hazard of restenosis and no material difference in periprocedural outcomes compared with CCSs. These findings support preferential consideration of OCSs at the carotid bifurcation for long-term patency, whereas CCSs may retain a theoretical advantage in unstable plaques requiring denser plaque coverage.

title: Endovascular reintervention versus conservative medical therapy for persistent or recurrent venous-origin chronic pelvic pain after primary ovarian vein embolization.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate and compare the clinical effectiveness of endovascular reintervention vs conservative medical therapy in patients with persistent or recurrent venous-origin chronic pelvic pain (CPP) after initial endovascular embolization for pelvic venous disorders (PeVDs). METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 79 patients with pelvic venous disorder and persistent or recurrent venous-origin CPP following primary ovarian vein embolization who subsequently received either reintervention (n = 40) or conservative medical therapy with venoactive drugs (n = 39). The primary endpoint was the 3-month CPP relief rate [Visual Analog Scale (VAS) reduction ≥2]. Secondary endpoints included longitudinal VAS score trajectories over 12 months. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to balance baseline covariates, and outcomes were analyzed using weighted logistic regression and Linear Mixed-Effects Models. RESULTS: The 3-month CPP relief rate was 67.50% (27/40) in the reintervention group and 35.90% (14/39) in the medical therapy group. After adjustment, reintervention group demonstrated significant overall superiority, with a more than threefold increase in the odds of 3-month CPP relief compared with medical therapy (odds ratio, 3.03; 95% confidence interval, 1.19-7.68; P = .022). The therapeutic advantage of reintervention was sustained through 12 months, with a significant group-by-time interaction (P < .001). Subgroup analyses showed no significant interactions for the 3-month CPP relief. However, significant interactions were observed for 12-month VAS improvement, with greater benefit from reintervention among patients initially treated at external institutions (P < .001) and those presenting with recurrence or partial relief (P < .001). No major procedure-related complications were observed during follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular reintervention-based strategy is an effective option for persistent or recurrent venous-origin CPP after initial embolization. However, therapeutic benefit varies across patient subgroups, highlighting the importance of individualized patient selection.

title: Association between intrinsic capacity, genetic predisposition, and risk of venous thromboembolism.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Association between intrinsic capacity (IC) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains unclear, we aim to explore the relationship among IC, genetic predisposition, and incident VTE. METHODS: In this large retrospective cohort study using the UK Biobank, IC, defined as the composite of all physical and mental capacities of an individual, was assessed across 7 factors (such as exhaustion, sleep duration, eye problems, hearing difficulty, weight loss, gait speed, and grip strength) and scored from 0 (best) to 7 (worst). Participants were grouped into five IC categories: 0, 1, 2, 3, and ≥4 factors. Incident VTE was identified through national medical records. Genetic predisposition to VTE was determined by the tertiles of polygenic risk score (PRS) derived from external genome-wide association data from the UK Biobank. Cox proportional hazards models were used to investigate the associations with multiple variables adjusted. RESULTS: A total of 415,581 participants (median age, 57.0 years; interquartile range, 50.0-63.0; 54.96% female; 94.89% White) were included in the final analysis. Over a median follow-up of 14.37 years, 8299 (2.00%) developed VTE, including 3878 (0.94%) with and 4421 (1.07%) without a history of cancer. Higher IC scores were associated with increased VTE risk compared to those with IC = 0 (for IC = 1: hazard ratio (HR), 1.08; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.16; P = .029; for IC = 2: HR, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.04-1.22; P = .005; for IC = 3: HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.06-1.34; P = .003; for IC ≥ 4: HR, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.23-1.75; P < .001). Similar associations were observed in both cancer and noncancer subgroups. Furthermore, individuals with both the highest PRS and the worst IC (≥4 factors) had the greatest VTE risk, with significant interactions between PRS and IC. CONCLUSIONS: Our large-scale study suggests that poor IC is an independent risk factor for VTE. Moreover, integrating IC with genetic risk can identify a high-risk subgroup, which supports the clinical utility of IC assessment in VTE risk stratification.

title: Rethinking IVC Filter Thrombosis Diagnosis: How Stratified Ultrasound Guidance Reshapes Endovascular Practice.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a precise, ultrasound-based stratification method for diagnosing thrombus within inferior vena cava (IVC) filters, aiming to optimize diagnostic accuracy and guide clinical decision-making regarding filter management. METHODS: This single-center study, conducted at the Emergency Orthopedics and Trauma Center of Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital, enrolled 323 patients from June 2023 to June 2025 who had undergone IVC filter placement and were suspected of filter-related thrombosis. Thrombus presence and characteristics within and around the filter were assessed using conventional ultrasound (grayscale and color Doppler) and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS). RESULTS: Based on the integrated ultrasound findings, patients were stratified into distinct management pathways: Class 0 (no thrombus) was detected in 258 cases, allowing for straightforward clinical planning. Class I/II thrombi (small, low-risk) were identified in 30 patients, enabling direct and successful filter retrieval. Class IIIa thrombi (larger, manageable) were found in 9 patients; CEUS guidance permitted careful intraoperative removal. The remaining 26 patients with Class IIIb thrombi (extensive, high-risk) received tailored treatments (eg, thrombolysis treatment, catheter placement) prior to subsequent filter removal. All filters were successfully retrieved, with surgical specimens confirming the ultrasound diagnoses. CONCLUSIONS: A stratified diagnostic approach using conventional and CEUS provides a reliable, noninvasive means to assess IVC filter thrombi. This method streamlines the diagnostic process, avoids unnecessary CEUS in clear cases, and delivers critical information for precise clinical decision-making in complex scenarios. By facilitating appropriate and individualized management plans, this approach can potentially improve patient outcomes and optimize filter retrieval workflows in emergency and trauma settings.

title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Risk for Thromboembolic Complication Among Patients With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and thromboembolic events among women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching. SETTING: Multicenter electronic health record database (TriNetX US Collaborative Network). POPULATION: Women aged 18-45 years with a diagnosis of PCOS between 2012 and 2021. METHODS: Women with PCOS were stratified according to subsequent diagnosis of OSA and matched 1:1 with PCOS patients without OSA using propensity scores. Incident pulmonary embolism (PE) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurring after a 1-year reference period were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Incident pulmonary embolism and venous thromboembolism. RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 20 052 women were included (10 026 per group). All analyses were conducted within this propensity score-matched cohort. PE incidence was higher among women with OSA compared with those without OSA (2.88 vs. 1.48 per 1000 person-years; absolute difference 1.40 per 1000 person-years; incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1.94, 95% CI 1.49-2.53; hazard ratio [HR] 1.95, 95% CI 1.50-2.54). VTE incidence was also increased (3.74 vs. 2.87 per 1000 person-years; absolute difference 0.87 per 1000 person-years; IRR 1.30, 95% CI 1.06-1.60; HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.07-1.61). These associations persisted across clinically relevant subgroups and increased over long-term follow-up. CONCLUSION: Among women with PCOS, comorbid OSA is associated with an increased risk of thromboembolic events, particularly pulmonary embolism. These findings support consideration of OSA screening and enhanced thromboembolic risk assessment in women with PCOS.

title: NDUFAF2 promotes abdominal aortic aneurysm formation through mitochondrial dysfunction-induced apoptosis.
abstract: in vitro In vivo 2 Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease closely associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis. Here, we found that NDUFAF2 (NADH dehydrogenase (ubiquinone) 1 alpha subcomplex assembly factor 2) was significantly upregulated in cultured cells and murine AAA tissues. Knockdown of NDUFAF2attenuated Ang II-induced mitochondrial fragmentation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and apoptosis in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), while improving mitochondrial membrane potential and oxygen consumption rate. In addition, NDUFAF2 knockdown reduced the expression of DRP1 (dynamin-related protein 1) while restoring the mitochondrial fusion protein OPA1 (optic atrophy 1), and OPA1 overexpression further enhanced mitochondrial integrity and function., NDUFAF2 knockdown suppressed CaCl-induced AAA formation, preserved aortic structure, reduced apoptosis, and restored mitochondrial complex subunits and smooth muscle cell markers. These results indicate that NDUFAF2 contributes to AAA progression by triggering mitochondrial damage and apoptosis, representing a promising therapeutic target for AAA.

title: Soft robotic devices for cardiovascular medicine.
abstract: Conventional, rigid simulators and therapeutic devices for cardiovascular disease have several fundamental limitations, such as poor biomimetic fidelity, substantial surgical invasiveness and mismatch at the tissue-device interface. Soft robotic devices, with tissue-like materials, structures and functions, are emerging as promising alternatives. In this Review, by matching clinical demands to technological breakthroughs, we identify three emerging complementary frontiers in which soft robotic devices are redefining cardiovascular medicine - soft robotic simulators, such as in vitro ventricular simulators and in vivo assistive simulators; soft robotic interventional instruments, such as percutaneous instruments, endovascular continuum instruments and untethered mini-scale robots; and soft robotic implants for vascular disease, arrhythmia and heart failure. We describe the unique advantages of soft robotic devices as well as their applicable scope and technical implementation. Finally, we highlight promising technological opportunities for next-generation soft cardiac devices, evaluate the clinical maturity of existing devices and propose a translational roadmap for the coming decade. With this Review, we aim to foster further integration of soft robotics into cardiovascular medicine by identifying device solutions with translational potential to address unmet clinical needs.
